top of page
Charles Sydney Wines Logo
Our Producers
Since the very start in 1990, CSW has been nurturing our relationships with many of the finest growers of the Loire Valley from source to sea. To this day, we employ the same rigorous selection procedure for any producer included in our catalogue – a task made all the easier as many of them are the finest producers in their appellations and are famous the world over.
There are a few criteria which apply to all our growers… Every single grower is acutely passionate and focused on growing the best quality grapes, thereby giving them the best chance of making the finest quality wines in their appellation.
Whether biodynamic, organic or HVE certified, all our hugely respectful of the ecology and environment of the land that they farm, and everyone is committed to investing in frost protection systems and doing everything possible to ensure that each year they can harvest the best quality grapes – or at the very least the best possible quality and volume that Mother Nature permits.
Investment continues in the cellars, where constant innovation is evident in experimental fermentation vessels, gravity fed wineries, state of the art presses and even growing yeasts specific to selected vineyard sites. The list is endless… We are extremely honoured to represent all the Loire growers on our list and are equally proud to consider them as friends as well as business partners.
Click here to read our catalogue
Domaine du Matin Calme
Anjou & the Coteaux du Layon
Domaine du Matin Calme was founded by Anne-Laura and Victor Robion, who met while studying oenology and viticulture at the Jules Guyot Institute in Dijon. Drawing on experience gained in Burgundy, Champagne, the Rhône, Loire Valley, New Zealand and South Africa, they established the domaine in Anjou with a clear vision: to produce precise, expressive wines that reflect their terroir. Based just south of Angers, the estate farms 16 hectares across a diverse range of soils including Loire alluvial sands and gravels, schist and volcanic rhyolite. Organically farmed and set to achieve organic certification with the 2025 vintage, the vineyards are managed with a strong focus on soil health and environmental balance. The domaine produces fresh, approachable wines alongside more terroir-driven single-plot cuvées. The range centres on Chenin Blanc and Cabernet Franc, with wines produced under Anjou Blanc, Anjou Brissac, Crémant de Loire and Coteaux de l’Aubance. Careful winemaking using both tank and barrel ageing preserves freshness, purity and a true sense of place.
Domaine de la Noblaie
Chinon and Bourgueil
Jérôme and his wife Elodie have been running the estate since 2003. Consisting of beautiful plateaus and clay/chalk hillsides, the vineyard shelters 20 hectares of Cabernet Franc and 6 of Chenin, the only varieties permitted in Chinon AOP. Jérôme’s wines gain in precision and fruit, proof that Cabernet Franc can ripen happily in the Loire Valley, giving rich, concentrated and complex wines.
Domaine la Bonneliere
Saumur
Domaine la Bonnelière is located in the town of Varrains, in the heart of the Saumur-Champigny appellation. The Domaine la Bonnelière covers an area of 42 hectares on the Varrains terroir. At La Bonnelière, the wines are made from the two main grape varieties of the Saumur appellation : Cabernet Franc and Chenin completed by 2 other complementary grape varieties: Cabernet Sauvignon and Pineau d’Aunis. The Bonneau family has obtained HVE certification, level 3, since 2020 and works the soil to naturally promote good vine growth. Their ethos is one of minimal intervention both in the vineyards and in the cellars.
Domaine Paul Buisse
Touraine
Paul Buisse's 100-year-old family négociant firm was based in cellars under the castle town of Montrichard on the Cher Valley - just upstream of the celebrated Chteau de Chenonceau. As well as working as a négociant, the firm owned its own vines - some 250 hectares split between Paul's original domaine in Pouillé and vineyards in the Touraine and Vouvray. Philippe Chainier has taken over the running of the estate, with his highly skilled brother François running the vineyards and vivifications – an impressive duo whose aim is to offer great quality and wonderful value. The Maison Paul Buisse works from an impeccably maintained cuverie and rock-hewn cellars and from a purpose-built winery set among the firm’s vines up above the Cher. Specialising in the classic Sauvignon Blanc of the Loire, the domaine wines are supplemented by buying-in grapes and juices which are vinified on site before bottling in Chainier's BRC-certified site in Amboise, allowing screw cap and even bag-in-box filling.
Caves de Pouilly Sur Loire
Pouilly Fumé
Set up just after the war, the Cave des Moulins à Vent has taken on a new and dynamic lease of life under the direction of Christophe Denoël and oenologist François Poirier, and is today producing Pouilly -Fumés of a quality to match the finest independent domaines. Christophe’s first priority was to get ISO and BRC certification, a move requiring considerable improvements in traceability and in management – and a great opportunity to put the Cave right back on a quality-oriented mode. Having substantially improved work in the winery and achieving ISO and BRC certification, the next major investment was in a screwcap bottling line, in 2015 they extended the whole building by a massive 40%, gaining bottling and storage facilities and increasing vinification capacity from 5,000 to 7,000 hectolitres, a reflection of the quality and success that the team are now achieving. Christophe has recently been concentrating on the vineyards, aiming to precisely identify soil-types so as to better vinify the appellation’s main terroirs. On a technical level, and with François’ aid, there have been equally dramatic improvements in selection of juice at the grower’s door and of vinification’s in the thermo-regulated stainless-steel vats of the Cave’s spotless winery.
Domaine des Herbauges
Muscadet
In the family since 1864, this medal-winning estate has grown under Jérôme Choblet is the 4th generation to run the domaine. Today, it has 107 hectares in production, with a further 30+ hectares under vine, making it the largest single estate in the Côtes de Grandlieu region. Furthermore, Jérôme has replanted 7 ha at the Chteau de la Pierre (totaling 16 ha) and has bought another 17 hectares at La Roche Blanche. In addition the estate also encompasses 260-hectare Côtes de Grandlieu Cru between the Muscadet Sèvre & Maine. More recently, he also took over a new domaine - Les 5 Chemins (12 Ha). In 2024, Jérôme also invested in a state-of-the-art canning line at the domaine. Exports have driven rapid growth, with 3 million cans and 1 million bottles sold in 2025. A second canning line will arrive by the end of 2026, supported by national retail agreements. Recognising growing demand for mid- and lower-strength wines, Jérôme recently launched a new 8.5% ABV range of White, Red, and Rosé made from expressive Grolleau Gris and Grolleau Noir. Light, fresh, and balanced, these wines deliver aroma and texture without compromise. Jérôme produces these wines entirely naturally—and we don’t believe you’ll notice the difference from a normal-strength wine.
Domaine du Clos Saint Martin
Sancerre
For more than four centuries, the Clément family has maintained a deep connection with the art of viticulture. Today, two generations of winegrowers work the estate, as Anne and Pierre-Alexandre pick up the torch from their parents. The Domaine du Clos Saint Martin is located below the village of Sancerre, near the hamlet of Amigny. The first traces of Clos Saint-Martin date back to 1650, when it was owned by the Priory of Saint Martin. The Clement family acquired the estate in 2020 which marks a new chapter for Clos Saint-Martin, the first harvest was made in 2023. The Clos Saint Martin vines stand on steep slopes that can exceed 40%. The terroir is distinguished by the presence of hard stones that are known as 'caillottes'. These soils benefit from very good natural drainage, they warm up quickly in spring, and reflect heat during the day and then release it during the night, thus promoting optimal ripening of the grapes. This geological particularity gives the Cléments’ Sancerre wines their unique identity and distinctive character: the true expression of the terroir.
Le Prieure De Saint Ceols
Centre
The history of this vineyard dates back to 1190, when land and vines were entrusted to the Abbey of Loroy. Later, Jacques Cœur, Grand Treasurer to King Charles VII, recognised the quality of the wines and helped bring Menetou-Salon to the royal table. The region’s soils originate from ancient marine sediments rich in limestone and fossilised shells, providing an ideal environment for both Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir. Established in 2020, Joseph and Marie de Maistre, who combine deep local heritage with the energy of a young, committed team, producing wines that are precise, authentic and firmly rooted in their terroirs. The estate covers 12 hectares, planted with 70 % Sauvignon Blanc and 30 % Pinot Noir, entirely farmed organically. The estate is farmed organically, with elements of biodynamic practice introduced across part of the vineyards. Viticultural and cellar interventions are deliberately kept to a minimum, allowing site and vintage to express themselves clearly.
Domaine Rethore Davy
Anjou & the Coteaux du Layon
The beautifully run vineyards of this 40-hectare estate are planted on the rolling hills of the Pays des Mauges - the broken metamorphic rock lying between Muscadet to the west and the Coteaux-du-Layon and the Anjou to the east. Set up in 1953 by Christophe Réthoré and Jean-Michel Davy's parents, the domaine has grown and evolved into one of the most carefully thought-out estates of them all. The Domaine continues to be passed down through the generations as Lise, Christophe and Martine’s daughter has joined the team in helping to run the estate. Benefitting from the lack of a regional AOC, all their vines are run to produce IGPs, so they can mix and match varieties to soil types as they please. Vignoble Réthoré Davy grows an extensive selection of both classic Loire Valley staples and varieties traditionally native to southern France. Their focus is heavily dedicated to pure, single-varietal expressions across their different collections. White Grapes varieties include: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay: Pinot Gris, Viognier, Chenin Blanc and Sauvignon Gris. Red Grape varieties include: Pinot Noir, Malbec, Syrah, Gamay, Cabernet Sauvignon and Abouriou. Committed to the welfare of the environment being Terra Vitis (responsible viticulture) and HVE (High Environmental Value) certification. The winery is certified organic as of the 2025 vintage, utilizing green manures and non-herbicide farming to cultivate these diverse vines.
Domaine de la Combe
Muscadet
Managed by fifth-generation winemaker Pierre-Henri Gadais, the Domaine de la Combe Vineyard spans 14 to 15 hectares. The entire vineyard is planted in a single block on a hillside called the Butte de la Combe. Formed of metamorphic rock layers consisting of schist, gneiss, and mineral-rich orthogneiss. Possesses a unique combination of young and old vines, with the oldest parcels planted in the 1950s. The estate completely halted chemical spraying in 2016 and earned its official Agriculture Biologique (Organic) certification with the 2021 vintage. Utilises a low-intervention approach with zero sulfur used during vinification, aging the wines "sur lie" (on the fine yeast lees) to add spritz, depth, and texture. Wines are are 100% Melon de Bourgogne, a historic variety that thrives in the local maritime climate.
Chateau de L Aulee
Touraine
Chteau de L’Aulée was built just outside Azay-le-Rideau by the Cordier family of Bordeaux. After a long history it was taken over in 2004 by Marielle Henrion, a Champagne-trained oenologist who had previously worked for Pommery, Bricourt and for some years with Bollinger. Today the estate has 30 hectares in production, including 20 of Chenin Blanc, 3 of Chardonnay, 1 of Grolleau with a further 6 ha in Chinon dedicated to Cabernet Franc grape for their crémant rosé. The vines are run according to the rules of La Lutte Raisonnée, with each plot being grassed through and run differently according to site and age of the vines. Concentrating on making sparkling wines always the mainstay of the Chteau’s production – Marielle picks the Crémants by hand in small caisses while the Touraines are picked with the latest generation Pellenc machine with its revolutionary built-in tri. Harvesting, vinification, bottling, ageing, riddling and disgorging are all carried out on the estate, which produces some 200,000.00 bottles per year, among which 85% are sparkling.
Domaine Charles Joguet
Chinon and Bourgueil
More than ably run under the direction of Anne-Charlotte Genet, Chinon’s most celebrated domaine now has 36 hectares of Cabernet Franc and 3 hectares of Chenin Blanc. With a committed move to organic vineyard management methods, the domaine continues to go from strength to strength as the team moves away from the belief that quality comes with mere concentration to search for an intensity and elegance of fully ripe fruit. The estate produces a stunning range of single-vineyard cuvées, each reflecting the particularity of its terroir and the age of the vines – over 80 years for the Dioterie. Maturation in oak is an essential part of the more intense cuvées and the new Charmes cuvée from old vines in the village of Anché (the plot is named after the local hornbeam trees) ferments in oak vats. The stars have always been the hugely ripe and balanced Varennes, Chêne Vert and the wine from the ancient vines of La Dioterie. Micro-oxygenation and careful barrel-ageing keep tannins soft behind the intensity and structure of these cuvées, arguably amongst the finest reds of the Loire.
Famillie Lebrumare Bernard Fouquet
Vouvray & Montlouis
Famille Lebrumare, Domaine des Aubuisières & Domaine De L’Arcadie & Bernard Fouquet range. The domaine comprises 29 hectares of Chenin Blanc planted on some of the best terroirs of the Vouvray appellation, enabling them to produce wines which exhibit all the richness, complexity and true potential of Chenin Blanc. Committed to making wines which have perfect balance and so in addition to our diligent vineyard management, they have also been converting to organic status since 2023. Using different vinification methods – oak barrels, stainless and clay amphoras – they are able to produce distinctly different styles of Chenin Blanc all of which showcase the richness and complexity of this noble grape.
